title: An operator can have what the files lack filled in from The Movie Database
description: Serves PRODUCT.md: "An operator who turns it on can have what those files lack filled in from The Movie Database: off until they do, the files always winning, nothing to upload by hand." (D-20261128-outside-metadata). Without it, a collection with no files beside its films has no synopses, artwork or photos of people, and an operator can't add them except one by one.
acceptanceCriteria: It is off until the operator turns it on with their own key, in configuration.
When it is on, each title's missing information, artwork and people's photos are filled in from The Movie Database automatically as titles are added; what files beside the film hold always wins.
To find a title, the server sends an identifier from its files when there is one, else its title and year, and nothing about who watches what.
The server fetches and serves the pictures itself; no viewer's device contacts The Movie Database.
An app can tell which titles show The Movie Database's data, so it can show the credit The Movie Database requires.
Nothing from The Movie Database is kept longer than six months: it is refreshed before then, and turning the feature off deletes all of it.
A title it can't match, or matches wrongly, is reported to the operator, who corrects it with an identifier in a file beside the film.
The Movie Database being slow or unreachable never holds up a scan, browsing or playback.
The operator documentation states what is sent, what is kept and for how long, and that The Movie Database's free use is for non-commercial use only.
The design states the storage, network and database cost for a collection of 10,000 titles.
notes: Octave must show The Movie Database's logo and its notice that the app is not endorsed by it; ask on Octave's board. Pictures follow D-20261128-picture-access: posters, backdrops and photos of people may be public.
